newsitem.title: MEXICO: Femsa beer unit 1996 sales volume higher.
newsitem.headline: Femsa beer unit 1996 sales volume higher.

text.p: Cerveceria Cuauhtemoc Moctezuma, the beer division of Fomento Economico Mexicano SA de CV (Femsa), posted sales volume of 21 million hectoliters in 1996, up six to seven percent over 1995, a company official said Tuesday.

"Beer sales in 1996 reached about 21 million hectoliters, an increase of six or seven percent compared to 1995," Ricardo Real Aguilar, director of Cevercia Monterrey, a subsidiary of Cuauhtemoc Moctezuma, told Reuters in an interview.
The Femsa unit, based in the northern city of Monterrey, is Mexico's second-largest beer company behind Grupo Modelo.
Cerveceria Cuauhtemoc Moctezuma has seven plants in Mexico and exports to 70 countries. Its brands include Sol, Tecate, Dos Equis and Carta Blanca.
Real Aguilar said he expected 1997 sales volume to grow four percent to five percent. Beer sales tend to rise in relation to the growth of the country's gross domestic product, he said.
Real Aguilar said the greater sales seen for 1996 and 1997 are largely due to the high number of Mexicans who are reaching drinking age in a relatively young country.
"We definitely expect the growth to happen (in 1997). We're thinking of extending the network and, of course, for the volumes to grow very aggressively," he said.
